items.title: Copper wire upgrade behind US flight suspension, transport secretary says
items.summary: The US government is trying to find out whether the chaos was caused by "incompetence" or faulty equipment.
items.content:
A nationwide US ground stop that caused thousands of flight cancellations and prompted travel chaos was caused by a technical issue following a copper wire upgrade, the transport secretary has said.

Sean Duffy told a news conference that the government was trying to find out whether the problem that led to air traffic controllers suspending take-offs for four hours on Friday had been caused by "incompetence" on the part of the company doing the upgrades or faulty equipment.

Though the ground stop was lifted on Friday evening, it had a knock-on effect on air travel on Saturday as airlines attempted to clear a backlog of flights.

Officials including Duffy had previously attributed the issue to outdated equipment.

Maintenance on US air traffic control systems was being carried out to switch from copper wire to fibre-optic cable by a contractor called L3Harris, a technology provider, Duffy said.

The US had "an incredibly old telecommunications system", he said, adding: "It was such an old wire that it was being discontinued."

The transport secretary explained that a router that was being worked on had started flooding other air traffic control systems and created communication issues with planes, prompting the shutdown on safety grounds.

The government was now trying to understand whether the root cause was the wire replacement or a fault with the router.

The four-hour suspension from 15:54 EST (19:54 GMT) on Friday was the longest such incident since the 11 September 2001 attacks on the US.

More than 15,000 flights in the US were delayed or cancelled that day, according to data from flight tracking sites, affecting an estimated 1.5 million passengers, with more than 5,900 cancelled and 7,000 delayed on Saturday.

In some cases, passengers were left stuck inside planes on the tarmac, unable to take off or to return to the gates. The ground stop also had a knock-on effect on schedules around the world, with some flights out of the UK and Europe cancelled.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said the US flight schedule should return to normal by the end of Sunday.

US officials have said they did not believe the issue was as a result of a cyber-attack or a rogue AI agent, though Duffy said an investigation into the exact cause was under way.

Bryan Bedford, who heads the FAA, told the same news conference: "We see zero evidence of anything nefarious and zero evidence of anything AI related."

L3Harris said on Saturday that it had completed more than 70% of the work it had been tasked to undertake to modernise US air traffic communications infrastructure before the shutdown.

The company said it was supporting the FAA in its investigation, adding: "L3Harris takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travellers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously."

Duffy warned that a similar issue could arise again unless the US Congress approved upgrades to air traffic control infrastructure.

US President Donald Trump has requested $30.1bn (£22.8bn) for the upgrades. Both chambers of Congress are currently controlled by the Republican Party.

Former TSA Administrator John Pistole told the BBC that "the fact that they were able to get it restarted in four-and-a-half hours is good news - it shows a resilience in the system - but what's to say it's not going to happen tomorrow?"

A nationwide ground stop has only been ordered one other time since all flights were banned from take-off for several days following the 11 September 2001 attacks.

A failure in the Notice to Air Missions (Notam) system in 2023 prompted a grounding that lasted an hour and 52 minutes, delaying about 9,500 flights and cancelling about 1,300.

items.title: Oppo Reno 17 e Reno 17 Pro, un leak svela tutto a un passo dalla presentazione
items.summary: I segreti ormai sono davvero pochi.
items.content:
All'ufficialità manca davvero pochissimo: ma Oppo Reno 17 e 17 Pro già oggi hanno pochi segreti. A un passo dal lancio fissato per domani, lunedì il 16 novembre, il noto leaker cinese Digital Chat Station ha anticipato gran parte della scheda tecnica dei due smartphone, rendendo ancora più completo un identikit che Oppo stessa in questi giorni ha contribuito a delineare anticipando alcune caratteristiche.

OPPO RENO 17

Reno 17 e Reno 17 Pro avranno tanto in comune, a partire da un design simile e una scocca con struttura in metallo, ma anche alcune differenze.

Nel dettaglio, Reno 17 standard sarà equipaggiato con un display LTPS piatto da 6,56 pollici, con risoluzione 1,5K. Sotto lo schermo troverà posto un lettore d'impronte ottico. Uno degli elementi più interessanti della scheda tecnica sarà la batteria da ben 8.000 mAh, abbinata ad una ricarica rapida cablata da 80 W.

Il medio gamma che accontenta tutti? Nothing Phone (3a), compralo al miglior prezzo da eBay a 299 euro.

items.title: Disk encryption on NetBSD – achieving secrecy
items.summary: Article URL: https://netbsd.org/~nia/disk-encrypt/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50504277 Points: 3 # Comments: 0
items.content:
These are two threat models for which disk encryption is the answer:

The device is stolen or lost and its contents must remain secret.

The device is tampered with, and all attempts at tampering must render it unusable.

Right now, we will focus on the first threat model. It is very difficult to build a tamper-proof system, and you need to worry about tamper-proofing your hardware, depending on what kind of actor is a realistic threat.

If we want to keep data on the system secret, we must first consider which data is worth protecting. On a NetBSD system, our data can be grouped into two broad categories:

Does the /bin/sh executable downloaded from the NetBSD FTP server contain any sensitive information?

On a BSD system, due to the separation of the base system and packages, many root file system directories are mostly unmodified outside of upgrades. In a properly configured system, nearly all system daemons and user applications are not going to be running as root , so won’t have permission to modify or create files in /bin .

We can reasonably assume that /bin/sh is the same binary that every other NetBSD user is running. A user may even opt to make directories containing such system files read-only.

The operating system needs to be able to load files to boot. [citation needed] This makes "true" full disk encryption difficult to achieve without specialized hardware, since the user needs some way to enter a password or an encryption key, and can’t do so without some form of software running on their computer. NetBSD also needs to store some amount of metadata about the encrypted partition on the disk, such as information on how to generate a secure 256-bit key from a 24 character password.

It is common for Unix systems to use shared libraries, which are loaded by programs to access system functionality. If these become unavailable, for example, by /usr/lib going missing, it becomes much harder to use the system. Familiarize yourself with the standard utilities in /rescue which don’t need working shared libraries to be useful.

The cryptographic algorithms that get standardized by the US government tend to be slow when implemented in software . This carries a performance penalty. As a result, many modern CPUs include implementations of ciphers like AES in hardware. For those that don’t, there’s alternative ciphers like Adiantum .

On a normal NetBSD system, several directories have a high chance of being modified during system operation:

/var - log files, system-wide databases (e.g. mail notifications), crash dumps…

/root - configuration files relevant to the root user account

/usr/pkg and /usr/local - where third-party software is installed

/etc - init scripts, system-wide configuration for the base system

A simple approach might be to encrypt /home . However, this might not be enough for some users. Although the crash directory can be easily changed with sysctl , a crash dump contains a snapshot of system memory which might be sensitive. If any servers have been run on the system, the log files might be sensitive. Mail sent to users (e.g. about their interrupted vi sessions and associated backups) might reveal sensitive file names.

Some users opt for the cgdroot approach, which uses only a small unencrypted ramdisk to pivot to an encrypted file system. However, this modifies the system startup routines significantly and may make certain rescue options harder. So, it’s worth asking whether there’s an approach that is somewhere in the middle, and still uses the standard NetBSD installation and boot process. Many BSD systems use separate file system partitions for /usr and /var , and this is a standard configuration supported by the NetBSD installer.

/etc is a harder problem to solve, since it contains files necessary to boot the system. However, on a typical desktop system, many files in /etc remain untouched. Passwords in /etc are generally stored only in hash form, except for Wi-Fi access points and certain VPN configurations (although it’s easy to reconfigure wpa_supplicant_flags to use a different configuration file from the default one in /etc ). Many configuration files are only loaded much later in the boot process, after /usr is already mounted, and can easily be replaced with symbolic links to files on another file system.

The NetBSD installer has basic functionality, but gets the job done quickly. In this configuration, we’re going to install NetBSD to a small unencrypted root file system. When you start to ignore the growth that can occur in /usr and /var and /home , even a complete NetBSD installation with development tools included is tiny. 4 GB should be more than enough.

For example purposes, I am going to use a sparc64 virtual machine, but the process is basically the same for more mainstream CPU architectures like amd64.

The installer detects that we already have a partitioned disk. We’re going to pick the "e: Delete everything" option so we have a fresh disk to start with:

Next, we’re going to choose "Set sizes of NetBSD partitions". This will allow us to have a small root, and reserve a large encrypted partition:

Here, I’ve decided I want a 4096 MB (4 GB) root file system, and a 11263 MB (11 GB) partition allocated for /var . Later, we’ll make /usr and /var share a disk partition, so don’t worry about this too much. Select "Go on".

On the next screen, I’ve changed the type of the secondary partition to "cgd" (listed under "Other type"), NetBSD’s encrypted device driver. I’ve also set its mount point to "-" so we can reconfigure it later:

I tell the installer I want to do a Full Installation and it completes as normal, installing everything into the small root partition.

When we reboot and log in as root , we enter a new world… our 4 GB unencrypted root partition.

Since I’m on sparc64, the disk is partitioned into disklabels. wd0 is the primary drive, and the disklabel command shows that /dev/wd0d is the partition reserved for our encrypted file system:

We can go directly ahead with creating a parameters file for the cgd :

Now cgd0 appears to the system as yet another disk, but all attempts to access that disk will be automatically encrypted/decrypted by the kernel.

The next time we enter our password, we want to be able to verify that the password was correct. This is done by choosing a verification method based on the contents of the encrypted partition. For flexibility’s sake, we’re going to put another disklabel inside the encrypted partition. This will allow the system to easily verify the password is correct by looking for a valid disklabel, but also gives us flexibility in our choice of file system.

This opens the interactive editor. We’re going to enter N to set a name for our disklabel (enter something like "cgdlabel"), then enter a to modify the first sub-partition.

First, it asks for a file system type. Enter ? to display a list of types:

Since I’m running -current and want to test the Log File System, I’m going to enter "4.4LFS". A more common and well-tested configuration would be "4.2BSD".

Since "a" is the only sub-partition at the moment, the default start of 0 is fine. "$" will use all available space on the cgd.

Finally, we’ll save our new label and quit the disklabel editor:

Now change the verify_method in /etc/cgd/wd0d to disklabel , and add a line in /etc/cgd/cgd.conf to create the cgd at boot time:

We can now access this hidden partition as /dev/cgd0a . But for it to be useful, we’ll need to create a file system on it. Once again, here I’m using the Log File System:

A more normal and well-tested configuration would be FFSv2ea:

Use "ffs" instead of "lfs" if you aren’t using the Log File System. If using FFS, you may want to use the options rw,log,noatime to enable journaling.

On a recent amd64 machine, your system probably uses GPT and disk wedges instead of disklabels. Assuming our primary disk is ld0 , we can see a list of wedges with dkctl :

In this case, our partition reserved for our encrypted file system is /dev/dk2 , also accessible via the UUID alias NAME=2c4d136a-f7ed-48f8-aae8-38afdd50c661 .

We can go directly ahead with creating a parameters file for the cgd :

Now cgd0 appears to the system as yet another disk, but all attempts to access that disk will be automatically encrypted/decrypted by the kernel.

The next time we enter our password, we want to be able to verify that the password was correct. This is done by choosing a verification method based on the contents of the encrypted partition. For flexibility’s sake, we’re going to put another GPT partition table inside the encrypted partition. This will allow the system to easily verify the password is correct by looking for a valid GPT table, but also gives us flexibility in our choice of file system.

Now change the verify_method in /etc/cgd/maincgd to gpt , and add a line in /etc/cgd/cgd.conf to create the cgd at boot time:

For now, we’ll only create one partition inside the new sub-table. I’m running -current and want to test the Log File System, so I’ll use the "lfs" partition type. A more common and well-tested configuration would be "ffs".

items.title: Wta Finals: Errani e Paolini volano in finale, battute Guo e Mladenovic
items.summary: La coppia azzurra conquista una storica prima volta
items.content:
Impresa del tennis italiano alle Wta Finals: Sara Errani e Jasmine Paolini conquistano per la prima volta in carriera la finale del torneo di doppio . Sul cemento di Indian Wells, in California , le azzurre hanno superato in semifinale la cinese Hanyu Guo e la francese Kristina Mladenovic in due set, con il punteggio di 6-3, 6-4, in poco più di un'ora.

Nella notte tra domenica e lunedì si giocheranno il titolo contro la ceca Katerina Siniakova e l'americana Taylor Townsend , già battute nella fase a gironi. Un percorso in crescendo per Errani e Paolini, che dopo aver dominato il proprio girone hanno confermato l'ottimo stato di forma anche in semifinale. Per le due italiane ora l'occasione di conquistare uno dei titoli più prestigiosi della stagione.

La coppia azzurra era stata l'ultima a qualificarsi per il torneo con la semifinale di Tokyo, dove poi hanno conquistato il loro primo titolo di stagione superando la coppia formata da Gabriela Dabrowski e dalla brasiliana Luisa Stefani.

items.title: Tennis's season finale takes centre stage in Turin
items.summary: The Piedmont capital has turned the ATP Finals, running from today until 22 November, into a citywide celebration. Only the world's top eight players qualify to compete for the final trophy of the year
items.content:
Turin is back at the net, confident it can win this match too. Unfortunately, Jannik Sinner is missing this time, but the ATP Finals remain the city's most important event of the year, alongside its International Book Fair.

Since the Piedmont capital took over as host in 2021, the season-ending championship has become much more than a sporting competition. It is now part of the city's identity, a magnet for tennis fans and a symbol of the golden age Italian tennis is enjoying. A boom that has helped bring the total number of registered players and Italians playing tennis and padel to more than 6.2 million.

Despite the significant absence of home favourite Jannik Sinner , who dominated the 2024 edition and reached the final against Novak Djokovic in 2023, this year's tournament promises plenty of tactical intrigue, compelling storylines and excitement.

First held in 1970 as the Masters Grand Prix, the ATP Finals have represented the ultimate showdown of the tennis season for more than half a century. Only the world's eight highest-ranked players earn the right to compete for the final trophy of the year.

From the eras dominated by legends such as Ivan Lendl, Pete Sampras and Roger Federer to that of record-holder Novak Djokovic, who has won seven titles, the tournament has always been a celebration of the very best.

For Turin, these five years in the spotlight of indoor tennis have brought genuine international recognition, despite the difficulties of the inaugural edition during the Covid pandemic.

The city has turned the tournament into a citywide celebration, with packed squares, cultural events, a Fan Village and thousands of enthusiasts arriving from around the world.

If Italian tennis is enjoying unprecedented popularity, much of the credit also goes to the energy generated by the Finals in the shadow of Turin's iconic Mole Antonelliana. And, of course, to the Sinner effect.

Alexander Zverev heads the draw, having officially taken the world No. 1 ranking from Sinner in the weeks leading up to the tournament.

The Finals hold special significance for the German, who has already won the title twice: in London in 2018 and in Turin in 2021. Arriving at the championship as world No. 1 makes him the man to beat, ready to rely on his consistency from the baseline and his devastating serve.

Despite sitting third in the rankings, Carlos Alcaraz is still the favourite. The Spaniard has the variety of shots and explosive power to dominate on any surface, with a style of play that is more spectacular than anyone else's.

Without Sinner to challenge him in the fast-paced rallies, Alcaraz is aiming to add the one major indoor trophy still missing from his collection.

Italian fans will certainly not be disappointed. Flavio Cobolli is ready to carry the hopes of the home crowd, following an extraordinary season that has propelled him into the world's top ten and secured his direct qualification for the Finals.

With his aggressive, athletic and electrifying tennis, the Roman is poised to become the tournament's dark horse and bring the Turin crowd to its feet.

The other contenders include Daniil Medvedev, the 2020 champion and always a threat on indoor hard courts; Ben Shelton, whose lightning-fast serve has helped him enjoy a season near the top of the rankings; Arthur Fils; Frances Tiafoe; and Spanish revelation Rafael Jodar. All are ready to upset expectations and deliver a spectacle.

The tournament's overall economic impact is estimated at around €590 million, almost six times the €103 million generated by the inaugural edition in 2021.

Direct spending in the city – on restaurants, hotels, transport and shopping – amounts to approximately €99 million.

The Italian state also benefits considerably. Tax revenues exceed €92 million, against a public contribution of around €13.7 million, leaving a substantial positive balance.

The event generates and sustains more than 4,100 jobs, with approximately €115 million in employment income supporting households.

And the arena is always packed, with or without Sinner. Between 200,000 and 230,000 tickets are sold over the tournament, running from today until 22 November, while hotels are reporting 98 per cent occupancy.

items.title: Virus RSV: drastico calo dei ricoveri
items.summary: Virus RSV: drastico calo dei ricoveri
items.content:
Vaccini e anticorpi monoclonali, le armi che negli ultimi anni abbiamo messo in campo contro il virus respiratorio sinciziale (RSV è la sigla più comunemente usata, dall'inglese Respiratory syncytial virus) stanno causando un calo in picchiata dei pazienti bisognosi di ricovero ospedaliero a causa del patogeno.
I dati che arrivano da Danimarca, Scozia, Argentina e Cile, sintetizzati in un articolo su Nature, fanno sperare che la lotta contro l'RSV possa giungere a un punto di svolta, una nuova stagione in cui i casi gravi possono essere evitati.. RSV: che cos'è e quali sono i sintomi. L'RSV è un virus altamente contagioso e molto comune che colpisce le vie respiratorie e la cui circolazione nel nostro Paese raggiunge di solito il picco tra gennaio e febbraio. Interessa con più frequenza i bambini nei primi anni di vita, ma può infettare pazienti di ogni età. In genere provoca i sintomi di un forte raffreddore, ma in alcuni casi può raggiungere le vie aeree inferiori e i polmoni, causando la bronchiolite acuta (cioè un'infezione delle piccole vie aeree o bronchioli) o la polmonite.. In base a una ricerca pubblicata nel 2025 su The Lancet Respiratory Medicine e che ha riguardato famiglie e servizi sanitari di Italia, Belgio, Paesi Bassi, Spagna e Regno Unito, l'RSV è responsabile di quasi un terzo delle infezioni respiratorie acute nei bambini.
L'OMS stima che ogni anno nel mondo vi siano 3,6 milioni di ricoveri per RSV e che il virus provochi la morte di circa 100.000 bambini di età inferiore ai 5 anni, per il 97% nei Paesi a basso reddito. Ma il virus è anche particolarmente pericoloso per gli anziani e per le persone già affette da malattie croniche.. Molte opzioni per proteggerci. Oggi per prevenire l'infezione da RSV si ricorre a vaccini da somministrare agli adulti a rischio e alle donne in gravidanza, e ad anticorpi monoclonali per i neonati.
In Italia sono disponibili tre vaccini contro l'RSV: vaccino ricombinante adiuvato, vaccino ricombinante bivalente e vaccino a mRNA. Il primo è indicato per gli adulti di età pari o superiore a 60 anni o per quelli nel decennio dei 50 anni particolarmente a rischio di malattia da RSV. Il secondo è adatto a tutti gli over 18 e in particolare alle donne in gravidanza, tra la 24esima e la 36esima settimana: gli anticorpi della madre oltrepassano la placenta e proteggono il neonato nei primi sei mesi di vita, quando è più vulnerabile all'infezione. Il terzo vaccino è indicato per gli adulti sopra i 18 anni.. Per i neonati e i lattanti non protetti attraverso la madre sono invece disponibili anticorpi monoclonali somministrati attraverso un'unica iniezione, che offrono quella che gli esperti definiscono immunizzazione passiva immediata: anziché stimolare attivamente il sistema immunitario, si legano al virus e gli impediscono di attaccare le cellule, offrendo protezione per l'intera stagione epidemica.. Cosa dicono i dati su vaccini e anticorpi contro l'RSV. In Danimarca, dove il vaccino contro l'RSV è offerto alle donne in gravidanza dall'autunno 2025, nella stagione epidemica tra 2025 e 2026 il numero di ricoveri ospedalieri per RSV di bambini tra 0 e 5 anni è calato del 75% rispetto alla media delle tre stagioni precedenti.
In Scozia, dove tra 2024 e 2025 il vaccino contro l'RSV è stato inizialmente somministrato solo nella fascia di età 75-79 anni idonea alla vaccinazione, il vaccino ha portato a una riduzione del 62% dei ricoveri ospedalieri a causa del virus.. In Argentina, la vaccinazione di donne in gravidanza ha portato a un calo del 34% dei ricoveri infantili nella zona di Buenos Aires. In Cile, la somministrazione ai neonati di anticorpi monoclonali contro l'RSV ha portato a un calo di ricoveri dei piccoli del 77%.
Secondo gli esperti, tempo e nuovi dati stabiliranno quali strategie siano più consigliabili per la protezione dei neonati. Vaccinare le madri è più economico, e gli anticorpi monoclonali sono ora usati per i neonati prematuri o per i bambini nati da madri con esitazione vaccinale. Intanto, organizzazioni come GAVI, l'Alleanza per i Vaccini, stanno lavorando per introdurre i vaccini contro l'RSV nei Paesi a medio e basso reddito..

items.title: Show HN: Gawain – Require type hints on all Python variables
items.summary: Yes, i really hate "dict[str, ANY]" Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50504072 Points: 34 # Comments: 12
items.content:
gawain requires type annotations on the variables, parameters, returns and class attributes of Python code, then runs a type checker, ty or pyrefly , to check that the types are correct.

Type checkers such as mypy, Pyright, ty and pyrefly infer the type of a variable that has no annotation. ruff's ANN rules and flake8-annotations ask for annotations on functions only. gawain also asks for them on variables and class attributes.

I built gawain only because I hate dict[str, Any] and wanted to do something about it. If your answer to this is "but Python already infers that" or "but my IDE infers it for me", then don't use it, little padawan.

retries = 3 passes, because a literal has an obvious type. PORT is a constant, so it needs Final[int] .

When every annotation is in place, gawain runs the type checker on the same files and prints what it reports. With ty, the default, for prices.py :

Install gawain with the extra of the type checker you want. ty is the default checker, and the ty extra pins it to 0.0.100:

To use pyrefly instead, install the pyrefly extra, which pins pyrefly 1.4.1 and does not install ty:

Then choose it with checker = "pyrefly" in [tool.gawain] , or with --checker pyrefly . docs/configuration.md explains the switch.

pip install gawain without an extra installs only the gawain command. It then needs a checker on PATH , or --no-types to run the annotation checks only.

Use gawain with care. ty is in beta, and its diagnostics may change between versions. If that is a problem for your project, use pyrefly, or --no-types to run the annotation checks only.

gawain exits with 0 when nothing is reported, 1 when it reports an error, and 2 on a usage error or when the type checker cannot run. The type checker's warnings are printed but do not fail the check.

GW000 marks a file gawain cannot read, and GW900 and GW901 mark a broken or unused suppression. To silence a line, name the code:

docs/rules.md has the full rules, the exemptions and the suppression syntax.

The default mode is obvious . A name may go without an annotation when its value has an obvious type and the name is never assigned again: a literal ( count = 0 ), a container of literals ( ids = [1, 2, 3] ) or a constructor call ( user = User("ada") ). strict asks for an annotation on every assignment:

pre-commit installs the hook from this repository's source, so building it needs Rust 1.97 or newer. docs/configuration.md covers [tool.gawain] , paths and the hook in detail.

On the CPython 3.14 standard library (1,847 files, 974,586 lines), median of 30 runs (5 for flake8-annotations):

gawain ran with --no-types . This is one benchmark on one machine (AMD Ryzen 7 3700X, WSL2). docs/benchmarks.md has the versions and the commands to run it again.

gawain reads Python with ruff_python_parser and checks types with ty, both by Astral , or with pyrefly , by Meta.

I don't know, I just like the Arthurian tales. Gawain is a knight of the Round Table, and the mascot is the Green Knight's axe with the green girdle from Sir Gawain and the Green Knight .

items.title: Show HN: Turbo-Browser-MCP – Batch forms, DOM deltas and submit guards for MCP
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/Tthanh2k6/turbo-browser-mcp Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50503930 Points: 26 # Comments: 4
items.content:
turbo-browser-mcp is a Playwright-based Model Context Protocol (MCP) server built to cut LLM token waste and multi-turn latency in browser automation. It consolidates 25-33 fine-grained browser primitives into 10 batched tools featuring delta DOM snapshots, single-turn React/Shadow DOM/iframe form prefill, direct disk file uploads (no Base64 in context), parallel tab sessions, network blocking presets, and a default human-in-the-loop Submit guard.

All figures below come from benchmarks/benchmark.mjs ( npm run benchmark ) running headless Chromium locally with exact OpenAI o200k_base tokenization ( tiktoken 0.14.0 ):

Note on latency vs LLM inference turns: Eliminating 10 round-trips on a 10-field form saves both 7x in browser execution ( 574 ms -> 82 ms ) and 10 separate LLM inference round-trips ( 2-5s per turn in agent loops) plus ~71,800 replayed history tokens.

Standard MCP servers charge an LLM round-trip for every snapshot, field fill, choice, upload, and verification check. Each turn re-sends the growing conversation history back into the model.

Prefills an entire form in one MCP call while flushing microtasks and macrotasks between controlled inputs:

Run the benchmark suite yourself with Chromium and Playwright installed:

Environment & methodology: Headless Chromium via playwright-core , counting exact OpenAI o200k_base tokens via Python tiktoken ( approx-bpe fallback if tiktoken is unavailable). Cumulative workflow tokens model standard chat-history replay across $N$ sequential turns: $\sum_{i=1}^{N} (N - i + 1) \cdot T_i$ , plus a one-shot baseline where the first turn captures context before acting.

Measured against installed MCP JSON schemas on disk (compact parameter schemas without annotations ):

When to keep Chrome DevTools MCP alongside turbo-browser-mcp : chrome-devtools-mcp provides Lighthouse audits, performance trace analysis, CSS computed style panels, and V8 heap snapshots. turbo-browser-mcp focuses on fast multi-step UI automation, forms, and scraping with minimal token overhead.

If you need Playwright's bundled Chromium (or have no system Chrome/Edge/Brave installed):

In Chrome 136+/144+, enabling chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging on the default User Data directory exposes a WebSocket in DevToolsActivePort that displays an "Allow remote debugging?" prompt whenever a new WebSocket client connects. turbo-browser-mcp provides two built-in solutions so overnight AFK multi-agent runs never hang on a prompt:

items.title: Cancellati sabato negli Usa 6.500 voli, oggi almeno altri 760
items.summary: Proseguono i disagi dopo lo stop di quasi 5 ore deciso venerdì dalla Faa
items.content: FlightAware, piattaforma che monitora il traffico aereo, ha segnalato 6.467 voli interni, in arrivo o in partenza dagli Usa cancellati nella giornata di sabato fino alle 21:30 locali (3:30 di domenica in Italia), mentre altri 760 risultano già soppressi per oggi. Venerdì, dopo il blocco del trasporto aereo di quasi 5 ore per i problemi alle comunicazioni deciso dalla Federal Aviation Administration (Faa), ne sono stati eliminati 9.202. Sabato, oltre 7.700 voli hanno subito ritardi: per oggi ne sono previsti 200. Delta Air ha cancellato sabato il 26% dei suoi voli, American Airlines il 42% e United Airlines il 26%, secondo la Cnn.

items.title: Judge temporarily blocks Trump from closing Washington DC golf course for renovation
items.summary: It is the latest development in a months-long challenge to the president's plans for East Potomac Golf Links.
items.content:
A federal judge has temporarily blocked the US government's closure of a historic golf course and park in Washington DC.

US District Judge Ana Reyes has been overseeing a months-long challenge to the president's plans for East Potomac Golf Links, which he said would be closed from 15 November for extensive renovations.

Reyes has said Donald Trump cannot close the park or its golf course, but added that his administration was not required to actively manage either.

Trump, an avid golfer, has said his plans to upgrade the 106-year-old course will create "one of the Best and Most Spectacular Golf Courses anywhere in the World". The BBC has contacted the White House for comment.

Declaring the current course "Trash Island", he announced in October it would be renovated over 15 months to create a space that "will be open to the Public while, at the same time, designed to the Highest Level of Golf and able to hold World Class Tournaments" - despite the ongoing litigation.

In a 30-page decision issued on Saturday, Reyes said the Trump administration's justifications for the proposed course closures were pretextual, and that the government violated at least two federal laws "to meet an arbitrary deadline."

"The Government proposes to close a historic park, daily enjoyed by Washingtonians of all stripes, indefinitely," Reyes wrote.

She said the closure "runs counter to the public interest in utilising national parkland", adding that the government had not "plausibly identified any harm it would suffer from a temporary restraining order that preserves the status quo pending further proceedings".

'Trash Island' or DC landmark? How a golf course got Trump in a messy legal dispute

The legal dispute dates back to February, when the DC Preservation League and others sued over redevelopment plans for the park.

The historic course, which sits 2 miles (3km) south of the White House, is one of three public courses run by the National Park Service in the nation's capital.

The legal fight then escalated in October, when the NPS began to cut down hundreds of trees without notifying Reyes until 15 hours before work was set to begin.

After the trees were cut, Reyes ordered the Trump administration to stop tree removal until at least 26 October and give her three business days' notice about making any other permanent changes.

Despite the work stoppage, Trump announced that the course would be closed for 15 months from 15 November to accommodate the renovations. He also shared a rendering of the course redesign.

"The current Course is old, broken, dilapidated, and of no further use or effect. It is in very poor condition, with falling, dangerous, and disease-infested trees and, importantly, a collapsing and hazardous seawall," he said in a post to Truth Social.

Reyes has since separately opened an inquiry into whether the justice department attorneys "have made misrepresentations to the court and otherwise violated ethical rules".

That included whether giving late notice to the court about the renovation plans was "done in bad faith" and whether the attorneys failed to correct previously false statements or withheld information.

She said she would carry out the inquiry with a special master, an independent third party.

Judge investigating whether Trump administration lied about golf course renovations

items.title: Pope Leo speaks of community 'suffering' on visit to remote Andes town
items.summary: Santa Cruz de Succhabamba is part of the Diocese of Chiclayo, where the pope served as bishop from 2015 to 2023.
items.content:
On a visit to an isolated Andean village in his former diocese, Pope Leo XIV has spoken about the "suffering of those who are forced to leave their homeland in search of a better future", which he said had left communities under threat.

About 6,000 people live in Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, which is located in a remote part of the Andes mountains in northern Peru, but the Pope's visit drew a crowd of about 20,000, according to the Vatican.

At an outdoor Mass, Pope Leo spoke of "declining birth rates that are emptying villages," and the unequal distribution of the land's resources.

Over 40% of the population in the Cajamarca region, where the town is located, live in poverty - the highest figure in Peru, according to official data.

Cajamarca has lost the highest number of people to internal migration, with 729,000 people born there now living elsewhere in Peru.

In his sermon, Pope Leo thanked those who had made the journey to him and emphasised the importance of never losing heart, despite life's difficulties.

Santa Cruz is within the Diocese of Chiclayo, where Pope Leo served as bishop from 2015 to 2023. During his tenure, he visited Santa Cruz several times a year to minister to the town's rural population.

On Saturday he returned by helicopter, where he was greeted by singing and cheering. He later did a tour in a popemobile, where he waved to people who had travelled from across the region to see him.

Speaking at a local parish on Saturday, the Pope said he felt "joy" at being able to visit the small town once again.

"It is like a very big dream that the Lord has allowed this servant to come here," he said.

Rev. Kevin Noriega, who was ordained in 2018 by the then-bishop, told Reuters the visit had brought "enormous hope and emotion" to Santa Cruz.

He said: "People are eager to experience this Holy Mass ... because after so much time they will be able to see their bishop - 'Father Robert,' as they used to call him - now as the Holy Father."

Peru is the longest stop on the first tour of Latin America by the leader of the Catholic church, who was elected in May 2025.

The 12-day trip has included stops in Argentina and Uruguay, but his time in Peru carries personal significance.

The US-born pope not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities.

The pontiff is set to leave Chiclayo on Sunday, when he will head to Cusco, and then on to a Peruvian sector of the Amazon rainforest. His tour of the region will conclude on Monday, at which point Pope Leo will return to Rome.

The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own

Pope begins lengthy trip to Latin America weeks after lung cancer surgery

items.title: My favourite modern NES games
items.summary: Article URL: https://jordi.inversethought.com/blog/25-of-my-favourite-modern-nes-games/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50503465 Points: 38 # Comments: 3
items.content:
We are in the middle of the Second ReNESance (the first one is the one that saved the video game industry in North America). The combined decades of research and knowledge on how the venerable little NES works have produced a true cornucopia of games. We are all lucky to be here to witness it.

I am always happy to inform video game fans that the Nintendo Entertainment System is still receiving lots and lots of new third-party games.

In alphabetical order, because I refuse to rank them, here are 25 of my favourite modern NES games. Almost all can be obtained digitally, usually from the developer or publisher, most for a modest fee. Digital NES downloads are cheap! Most of these can also be obtained as physical cartridges for the true hi-fi experience on original hardware.

Made by 8-bit Slasher who has been honing his skills in other horror games for the NES, All Hell Unleashed is an extensive love letter to the horror slashers of the 1980s and 1990s. There is an underlying story about an evil cult that is trying to resurrect something or other, but that’s just an excuse plot so that you can fight Jaws, Freddy, Jason, Ghostface and others. It works surprisingly well. You can select your favourite horror movie from a stage-select screen to do your platforming as you fight the forces of evil, culminating in the boss fights where the villain of each horror franchise swoops in for a mano-a-mano . The platforming feels good, and the boss fights function as set pieces showcasing the real villains we are here to see in their 8-bit glory.

Finally Jason dons a better outfit on the NES than that silly purple jumpsuit!

After each classic horror villain is defeated, it is time to take on the cult itself for one final showdown. Definitely a spine-tingling adventure!

Alwa’s Awakening was originally a PC game made with pseudo-NES limitations (and in the case of the music, with actual NES limitations, as the developer used Famitracker to compose all of the music). If it doesn’t feel like a classic NES game and instead plays more like a modern indie Metroidvania, that’s because it is.

In the game, you play as Zoe, a girl who likes video games and one day awakens in the mystical land of Alwa, a place from one of her games. Your task is to guide Zoe through an adventure in Alwa where she will uncover power-ups that open up new avenues of adventure. Typical Metroidvania stuff, although a bit shorter than most games in the genre. The PC-to-NES port of this game was handled by my good friend Brad Smith of Lizard fame. He made a couple of interesting YouTube videos describing the process.

The game looks absolutely gorgeous for the NES, and its Famitracker-composed soundtrack made it through the porting process completely unscathed. There was a limited physical edition that today is only available via secondhand markets. If you can grab a copy, it’s a very high-quality production. This is some of the best stuff made for the system.

Anguna is an NES game with an interesting lineage. It was originally made in 2008 for the Game Boy Advance as essentially the same game, but a bit more to the standards of the GBA. Then it was successively ported to the Nintendo DS, the Atari 2600, and finally the NES.

The Atari 2600-to-NES port was done fairly faithfully, which means that the design decisions necessary for the Atari also made it into the NES port. This means, for example, no more than two enemies per screen and always of the same type. This sort of restriction isn’t unheard of in the NES, though. The very popular NES Double Dragon port also has the same limitation. The game design makes up for it and overall results in an enjoyable experience. And isn’t that what making and playing modern NES games is all about? An interesting experience made with strict hardware limitations.

So what is Anguna? At its most basic, it’s a Zelda-like. You walk around screens, you grab new tools, your tools open new paths for exploration, you use the tools to fight monsters, with the most common tool in question being your trusty sword. You are a nameless warrior who is notably NOT called “Anguna” on a quest to defeat the goblin king. Usual bare-bones plot.

Most might consider this game to be short, but I would say it’s sleek and streamlined. It doesn’t do much, but what it does it does well.

Oh, one very important upgrade that the game got during the 2600-to-NES conversion: rockin’ enemy portraits in gorgeous 8-bit pixel art!

Blazing Rangers is single-screen arcade firefighting co-op action! The firefighting genre is under-explored in video games and Blazing Rangers manages to represent it admirably.

The goal is to rescue the children in each burning level and proceed to the next one. To do this you have to snake a powerful firehose that can blast both flames and baddies as you make your way to the children. You may also and often must drop your firehose and rely on your backpack with water in order to get to the further reaches of each level. There are powerups to collect, which give bonuses such as increasing the length of the hose or activating a sprinkler system that will slow the spread of fire throughout the level.

You can control either of two characters, Popo and Mimi, each with slight differences in gameplay. Popo is a bit slower but can recharge his backpack with water faster while Mimi is the other way around. Each level is timed, but you’re more likely to be overrun by flames or enemies than running out of time. The children can get singed by the fire but otherwise seem unharmed, unless you get burned carrying them, in which case they get burned too.

The game has a very catchy theme song that is also the BGM of each level.

Although it can be fun enough in single player, co-op is where the game really excels. It is very fun to coordinate with your partner as there is still only one hose in co-op. A strategy, for example, could be to have one player get the hose extension powerup that the other player can instantly use to take the hose a bit further into the flames.

Estique is a horizontal shmup with the distinct honour of being made by some of the original Compile developers, veterans of the shmup genre. This is noticeable in that it even uses some sound effects from Compile classics such as The Guardian Legend . In the game you pilot the eponymous super-robot that can transform between the bipedal mecha form that can recover damage more quickly or a sleek spaceship form that is more manoeuvrable and has a faster firing rate. Gameplay consists of carefully balancing between the two forms in the heat of battle depending on whether a more offensive or defensive approach is needed at the time.

The NES manual has a deliberately awkward English translation as a homage to the quality of writing we often encountered during the licensed era. Accordingly, the Japanese and English versions of the game are not identical, with the English version having mild censorship of the cut scenes, mimicking the restrictions that Nintendo used to impose on licensed NES games.

The game’s default difficulty is a little on the easy side, and the whole game can be completed in under an hour at the default difficulty. I get the impression that the intended difficulty is a bit higher, so you can always adjust it up for your gaming needs.

Regardless of the difficulty, the giant screen-filling boss fights are always a delight.

Why 2nd adventure, you might ask? Well, this game has an interesting history . The original adventure was written way back in 2015 to support the Arc of Cowlitz County charity. Within a couple of years, a sequel appeared and physical copies were made and distributed at the Portland Retro Gaming Expo. They aren’t made anymore, but if you’re exceedingly lucky, you might be able to nab a second-hand copy somewhere. Finally the game was uploaded to itch.io as a free download, with a nudge to donate to the charity.

The game is a tightly-made single-screen arcade platformer where siblings Kaylee and Justice decide to go down into the mines and see who can collect the most gold and diamonds to buy fireworks for the festivities. It can be played co-op or single-player, where the co-op is also half competitive mode to see who can pick up the most gems. The siblings have no way to directly attack any of the enemies in the mines, so it’s all up to careful jumping and dodging to clear each screen of gold in order to open the way up to the next screen.

The platforming is responsive and engaging. Very fun to play. It’s no surprise then that this game has achieved some popularity with speedrunners .

The music is a real standout and full of earworms. Several chiptune artists contributed to this game’s vibrant soundtrack. I often find myself humming the tune of the first few levels. Sometimes I even go into the options screen where the sound test lets me play all of the game’s tunes and use it as my jukebox.

The game’s colourful graphics perfectly complement the music.

Okay, before we go on, I have to point out this game’s hilarious retro-themed trailer.

items.title: Guerra in Iran, le news di oggi. Esplosioni in Bahrein, Iran rivendica attacco contro base radar Usa
items.summary: Il Ministero dell'Interno del Bahrein ha invitato i cittadini a recarsi nel luogo sicuro più vicino per garantire la propria incolumità
items.content:
L'iran ha rivendicato alcuni attacchi contro una base radar degli Stati Uniti in Bahrein . Alcune esplosioni sono state udite nel Paese del golfo e sarebbero riconducibili all'attività di droni: secondo quanto riporta l'Afp, sono risuonate le sirene d'allarme e le autorità hanno diffuso diversi messaggi di avviso sui social network, invitando la popolazione a raggiungere un luogo sicuro, senza tuttavia specificare la natura della minaccia.

In un messaggio pubblicato su x, il ministero dell'interno del Bahrein ha esortato "i residenti a mantenere la calma, a recarsi nel luogo sicuro più vicino e a seguire gli aggiornamenti attraverso i canali ufficiali".

L'attacco è stato rivendicato dai Guardiani della rivoluzione , che hanno reso noto di aver attaccato una base militare statunitense. "Il sistema radar della difesa aerea statunitense presso la base per elicotteri di Al-riffa, in Bahrein, è stato preso di mira da sei droni appartenenti alla forza aerospaziale dei guardiani della rivoluzione islamica", hanno dichiarato i pasdaran in un comunicato diffuso su Telegram.

I Guardiani della Rivoluzione hanno attaccato con dei droni una base militare statunitense in Bahrain. "Il sistema radar della difesa aerea statunitense presso la base per elicotteri di Al-Riffa, in Bahrain, è stato preso di mira da sei droni appartenenti”, hanno dichiarato i Guardiani in un comunicato su Telegram. Poco prima, nel paese del Golfo erano risuonate le sirene d'allarme.

"Le difese aeree hanno intercettato e distrutto due missili balistici lanciati dalla milizia terroristica Houthi verso Riad". Lo ha scritto su X il portavoce della coalizione guida saudita che combatte contro gli Houthi in Yemen, Turki al-Maliki. In precedenza, in altri post, aveva reso noto che le difese aeree saudite avevano abbattuto due droni nella regione orientale del Paese.

items.title: We're Asking an Appeals Court to Require a Warrant for ALPR Searches
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2026/11/were-asking-appeals-court-require-warrant-alpr-searches Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50503255 Points: 198 # Comments: 53
items.content:
Today , along with the ACLU, EFF filed an amicus brief in the Sixth Circuit court of appeals in United States v. Sturdivant , a case where police warrantlessly tracked a suspect’s movements using Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) data. Our brief details the vast, interconnected network of ALPRs that constantly track drivers around the country and argues that this tracking is a “search” under the meaning of the Fourth Amendment.

Sturdivant involves a series of robberies in and around Cleveland, Ohio. Using surveillance camera footage, police identified the make, model, and color of the robber’s car, but they did not know its license plate number. After running an open-ended search of two ALPR databases, Flock and ELSAG, officers learned a car belonging to the defendant had been tracked near sites of the robberies, eventually leading to his arrest. Faced with a motion to suppress the ALPR evidence, the district court held that Mr. Sturdivant had no reasonable expectation of privacy in his license plate number because it could be observed by members of the public, and that therefore he had no Fourth Amendment interest in not having his car tracked in public places.

But ALPRs are simply not comparable to observing an individual license plate on a passing car. As we’ve explained in many amicus briefs and in our lawsuits directly challenging ALPR use in San Jose, California and Wisconsin , ALPRs give law enforcement “ a virtual time machine to view suspects’, or anyone else’s, past movements (and much more) with just the click of a button.” Just last month, a federal district court agreed and held that ALPRs are a “ form of indiscriminate mass surveillance” that can violate the Fourth Amendment.

We hope the Sixth Circuit will reverse the lower court in this case and hold that ALPR searches require a warrant.

items.title: Court denies motion to dismiss DRAM price fixing case
items.summary: Article URL: https://litnews.ai/articles/garciaguirre-samsung-sk-hynix-micron-dram-conspiracy-suit-survives-dismissal Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50502988 Points: 71 # Comments: 16
items.content:
A federal judge on Nov. 14 declined to dismiss a proposed class action accusing Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron of conspiring to restrict the supply of conventional dynamic random-access memory, or DRAM, the chips that provide temporary, high-speed data storage in computers, phones and servers.

U.S. District Judge Noël Wise of the Northern District of California denied the companies' joint motion to dismiss, finding the complaint plausibly alleged an agreement in violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act. The allegations, accepted as true at this stage, have not been proven.

The companies argued the case was a rerun of In re Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) Indirect Purchaser Antitrust Litigation, or DRAM II, in which the Ninth Circuit in 2022 affirmed dismissal of claims against the same three companies over a 2016–2018 supply restriction. "The Court finds that it is not," Judge Wise wrote, though she sided with the companies on several theories.

The suit was filed June 25, 2026, by 17 consumers and small businesses from five states. According to the complaint, the three companies controlled more than 91% of global DRAM revenue as of the third quarter of 2025 and cut production beginning in late 2022. The suit asserts a Sherman Act claim and claims under the laws of California, Florida, Minnesota, New York and Wisconsin, which the parties agreed rise and fall with the federal claim.

The complaint alleged the companies then shifted capacity to high bandwidth memory, or HBM, a specialized, stacked form of DRAM used in artificial intelligence accelerators, and between April and June 2025 announced they would wind down mainstream DDR4 production. It alleged a 697% price increase over 18 months, yet none of the companies meaningfully expanded conventional capacity.

Without direct evidence of an agreement, the plaintiffs had to allege more than conscious parallelism, the lawful practice of competitors in a concentrated market independently making similar moves. That requires plus factors, additional facts suggesting a preceding agreement.

Judge Wise rejected the companies' argument that timing gaps undercut parallel action. SK Hynix and Micron announced cuts three weeks apart in late 2022, she noted, and Samsung's lag of about four and a half months, until April 7, 2023, was "not such an unreasonably long delay that it defeats an allegation of parallel conduct on a motion to dismiss."

She found parallel conduct in the supply cuts, the HBM pivot and the DDR4 exit but set aside the DDR3 allegations, because the complaint admitted Micron kept producing DDR3, conduct she called "neither parallel temporally nor parallel in kind."

She also agreed with the companies that the HBM pivot alone was insufficient, since the complaint itself alleged HBM was more profitable when the shift began. Under the Ninth Circuit's decision in In re Musical Instruments and Equipment Antitrust Litigation, action against self-interest must be "so perilous in the absence of advance agreement that no reasonable firm would make the challenged move."

But according to the complaint, all three signed long-term contracts locking in HBM supply, Samsung and SK Hynix reportedly refused long-term agreements with major conventional DRAM customers, and Micron announced on Dec. 3, 2025, that it would close Crucial, its 30-year-old consumer brand. Those moves, plus the failure to expand despite record prices, "are the sort that at the pleading stage, it appears no reasonable firm would make without a prior agreement," she wrote.

She applied similar reasoning to allegations that Samsung and Micron delayed or halted new DRAM plants, citing a 1990 Ninth Circuit ruling in a petroleum case that "Changes in refinery capacity are not readily reversible." "The Court views the commitment to build or not build manufacturing capacity as analogous," she wrote.

On DDR4, the companies argued they "exited that product on different timelines," but the complaint alleged all three decided within the same quarter while DDR4 "remained in wide use." Apart from pointing to increased Chinese production without citing the complaint, the judge wrote, the companies "offer no rationale for their sudden, rapid, and coordinated exit from DDR4." Their assertion that they feared Chinese competition, she added, "is not in the complaint."

Judge Wise found that near-identical customer-vetting questions all three companies allegedly adopted in January 2026 "strongly support a plausible inference of conspiracy." She rejected the companies' "obvious and non-conspiratorial explanation" of booming AI demand, noting that the vetting began in January 2026, years after the AI boom and the HBM pivot began. She also rejected their argument that the plaintiffs never alleged any exchange of vetting information, writing that requiring such direct evidence "is not the standard."

Other theories did not help the plaintiffs. The judge held that the companies' public statements to investors did not distinguish the case from DRAM II, which found similar statements insufficient. She found the plaintiffs' allegations about industry-conference meetings went further than those in DRAM II but declined to rely on them, writing that DRAM II "seemingly all but forecloses a trial court from giving any weight to trade conference meetings" unless plaintiffs identify what was actually exchanged. She called the market's oligopolistic structure "neutral in the analysis."

According to the complaint, the companies and two other manufacturers formed a criminal cartel to fix DRAM prices from 1998 to 2002; Samsung paid a $300 million fine, Hynix paid $185 million, and Micron received immunity as a cooperating whistleblower. The companies argued that now-20-year-old history should not count, but Judge Wise, like the DRAM II court, rejected that argument.

At the hearing, the companies quoted the late Judge Posner's line that competitors in concentrated markets "watch each other like hawks." Judge Wise wrote: "But Plaintiffs' allegations go beyond hawks watching each other; their contentions are more akin to hawks flying in formation – an activity that hawks ordinarily do not do."

The plaintiffs are represented by Bathaee Dunne LLP. Samsung is represented by O'Melveny & Myers LLP, SK Hynix by Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton LLP, and Micron by Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP.

Judge Wise ordered the companies to answer by Dec. 7, 2026. Because the court had reset argument by about three weeks, she also granted the companies' unopposed administrative motion to continue early case deadlines and reset the initial case management conference for Jan. 12, 2027, at 9 a.m.

items.title: Scopri la nuova gamma di QD-Mini LED di TCL: il vero local dimming al giusto prezzo
items.summary: Oltre alla rivoluzionaria gamma SQD-Mini LED, TCL offre quest’anno anche modelli QD-Mini LED versatili e dall’ottimo rapporto qualità/prezzo, tutti con vero local dimming e funzionalità complete ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Con la tecnologia SQD-Mini LED, TCL ha ridefinito la nuova frontiera del colore, ma per chi cerca ottime prestazioni con i contenuti di tutti i giorni e il miglior TV al miglior prezzo, TCL propone anche una solida gamma di televisori QD-Mini LED , con efficace tecnologia local dimming per immagini luminose e dall’elevato rapporto di contrasto, e ampia gamma cromatica grazie ai quantum dot. Per rispondere alle diverse esigenze di spazio, budget e utilizzo, TCL ha declinato la sua tecnologia di punta in tre proposte ben distinte, mantenendo ferma la promessa di un vero local dimming accoppiato alla purezza dei Quantum Dot, con le nuove serie A400U, C6K Pro e P8L. Con soluzioni che vanno da 55 pollici su fino ai 98 pollici, TCL offre quest’anno un ampio ventaglio di modelli, tutti basati su Google TV, con supporto per i principali formati HDR incluso Dolby Vision, audio Dolby Atmos firmato Onkyo e funzioni complete. La gamma è già disponibile in promozione su Amazon , ma vediamo nel dettaglio tutti i nuovi modelli QD-Mini LED.

La nuova serie TCL A400U è la scelta ideale per chi cerca l'eccellenza visiva senza scendere a compromessi con il design.

Caratterizzata da un raffinato design “wallpaper” estremamente sottile che si integra perfettamente a parete, la serie A400U è disponibile nei tagli da 55”, 65”, 75”, 85” e persino 98” ed è dotata di caratteristiche tecniche di alto livello:

items.title: My mother told me I would die if I sought treatment for Ebola - I am proof you can survive
items.summary: Fear and misinformation surrounds the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo - Dr Kamwanga's mother was not immune.
items.content:
When Dr Raymond Kasereka Kamwanga told his family he suspected he had Ebola and was going to a treatment centre in the city of Butembo in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, his family were horrified.

They regarded the specialised unit as a "death house" as not many patients do recover - especially those admitted in the late stages of the illness. His 50-year-old mother was in tears, pleading with him not to go there.

"Why are you choosing to die at the Ebola treatment centre?" Masika Ndungo had asked him.

But as a doctor at Butembo's Katwa Hospital, he knew that if stayed at home, he was unlikely to survive.

This was in July, two months after the World Health Organization (WHO) had declared the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo a public health emergency of international concern. Since then 5,400 people have died and 11,000 have been infected, making it the second-most deadly outbreak ever recorded.

Butembo is in North Kivu province, the epicentre of the crisis, with the highest number of reported cases, according to the Congolese health ministry.

Dr Kamwanga is one of 3,031 people who have survived - and is evangelical about sharing his story in an effort to help stop the spread of infections devastating his community.

After staring death in the face and overcoming ostracisation, he has even started writing a book about his experience.

"As someone who has recovered, I am living proof that the disease exists, but also that it is possible to recover from it," he tells the BBC outside Katwa Hospital where he still works.

The 30-year-old medic believes he contracted the virus through contact with a patient in a setting where protective measures are not always adequate.

The first symptoms appeared gradually: a bitter taste in his mouth, headaches and a general feeling of malaise. He contacted the Ebola response team.

After an initial consultation and some tests, he returned home, but his condition did not improve.

Butembo does not have the equipment to quickly test for Ebola - samples need to be sent to the city of Beni, 54km (33 miles) north.

This delays diagnosis as the condition of roads in this war-torn and underdeveloped part of DR Congo means it can take between 48 and 72 hours to travel even this relatively short distance.

After three days at home, Kamwanga felt extremely weak and experienced muscle pain. On the fourth day, he began vomiting and had diarrhoea.

This is when he gathered his family members - including his mother - to tell them he had to go to the Ebola treatment centre.

"She had started crying, along with my sisters. I told them everything would be alright, that I was a doctor and that I was confident. But they weren't reassured," he says.

Around 18:00, he set off on foot to the nearby centre but refused to use the main entrance.

He called his colleagues and asked them to put on their protective gear before they approached him and isolated him. The virus spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids.

The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment.

"The treatment given to Ebola patients is symptomatic - meaning that doctors treat the symptoms the patient presents," says Kamwanga, explaining that in his case it was severe vomiting and diarrhoea.

In some patients these symptoms can lead to organ failure and then some develop internal and external bleeding.

Kamwanga lost a lot of fluid and struggled to stay hydrated - he was terrified.

"I was afraid for myself. Every day, patients were dying right before my eyes. But I stayed positive," he explains.

Over 13 days lying in his hospital bed, he tried to keep his spirits up by watching movies and TV shows on his phone, reading and scrolling through TikTok.

The day he learned he had recovered, Kamwanga felt immense relief. He thanked the healthcare workers who had cared for him.

However, even a certificate showing he was Ebola-free did not initially dispel the unease those around him felt after he was discharged.

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

'I buried my parents one day after the other' - Ebola mourners learn how to grieve safely

"We welcomed him home warmly. But because of our fear, we didn't get close to him any more," Ndungo, his mother, tells the BBC.

For 21 days - the incubation period of the virus - the doctor lived separately in another part of the family home, which was crowded at the time with at least 18 people living there, including several children and people displaced by recent fighting in the region.

He would only see them from afar when he went to pick up his meal, while other family members kept their distance.

"We were really afraid, but we prayed to God to protect him at the treatment centre. With God's help and the doctors' efforts, we saw him return in good health," she tells the BBC.

They all agree the experience changed their perception of Ebola.

Some do not believe the disease even exists - Ndungo says that witnessing Ebola first-hand helped to dispel some of that misinformation.

After his recovery, Kamwanga threw himself into community outreach - sharing his story as a way of combatting rumours and mistrust.

"I started writing my book - The Price of Saving Lives - one week after recovering and leaving the hospital," he says. "However, it is not finished yet. What I currently use during my awareness-raising activities is the draft, and it is already making a significant impact."

During these sessions, he also distributes photos taken while he was sick to help convince residents that Ebola is real.

But in Butembo, this mission remains difficult. Kamwanga explains that some people view awareness campaigns as a way for humanitarian organisations to profit from donor funding.

Such mistrust, which is also levelled at healthcare professionals, is often fuelled by poverty and trauma related to years of armed conflict, he says.

"Ebola has come alongside the war," he says, explaining that some even interpret it as a way for those in authority to threaten a vulnerable population "to finish off those whom the war failed to exterminate".

He also believes that the number of deaths observed during epidemics - compared to recoveries, which are sometimes less visible - reinforce fear and suspicion.

But putting himself on the front line also comes with risks - and Kamwanga says he receives death threats on his phone.

Some residents accuse him of being paid to spread information about Ebola. He also reports that outreach workers have been attacked by members of the community.

He feels the authorities do not work effectively to address all these problems: "Our government is taking things lightly."

He agrees too with the recent report by Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) that Ebola funds are going missing .

"The money allocated to the Ebola response is being misappropriated by the government. We do not have enough protective equipment," the medic says.

Despite the intimidation and the obstacles he and other medics face, he remains determined - his goal is to help put an end to the disease.

"Should we give up the fight against Ebola? No. We continue to do what we can with the resources available to us, which are unfortunately very limited."

items.title: Judo champion shakes up French presidential race with surprise candidacy
items.summary: Teddy Riner is one of the most popular figures in modern-day France, and one in five voters say they could support him.
items.content:
Apart from an overwhelming urge to pin one's opponent to the floor of the house, there is no obvious connection between politics and the world of top-level judo.

That has not stopped France's much-garlanded world heavyweight champion Teddy Riner from throwing his hat into the ring for next April's presidential race.

The Guadeloupe-born 37-year-old may have no experience of public office, no party behind him, and as yet no manifesto. All so far is a slogan La France qu'on aime (The France we love), a declaration on social media, and a campaign visit to a hospital in the Seine-Saint-Denis suburb of northern Paris.

But it would be a foolhardy pundit who would totally write off his chances.

Riner is, after all, one of the most popular figures in modern-day France, regularly topping the polls for embodying the nation's "values". He is a proven winner, with five Olympic golds and 11 world championships under his belt, as well as a successful career in business.

More than 28 million people have watched his election broadcast on Instagram and X, shot with proper presidential decorum against a backdrop of books and a French flag. Some 22% told an Ifop poll within 24 hours they "could" vote for him.

Actors and television personalities have become presidents in other countries. The ex-leader of Liberia – George Weah – was formerly a professional footballer.

"Anyone who thinks that being out of the political in-crowd disqualifies Riner from running for the Élysée would be very wrong," says Guillaume Tabard of Le Figaro.

"But [Riner] too would be wrong if he thinks not belonging to the in-crowd is all it takes."

For now the whole of the French political world has decided to take the Riner candidacy seriously – or at least to pretend to. That is partly because he is such a popular personality that mocking his political hopes could easily rebound badly.

But it is also because the state of French politics – outside of the burgeoning forces of the hard left and hard right – is one of total disarray.

The centre-ground is floundering, with no candidate yet emerging who can inspire anything like the sense of mission of hard-right leader Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon on the hard left, who for now look set to face off in the final round of the presidential election in May.

So when a popular figure like Riner enters the race - proclaiming himself "neither left, nor right", wanting to "unite the country" and "put money back in people's pockets", railing equally against "racists" and "yobs who scare people off our streets" – politicians have to take note.

It is perfectly possible, probable even, that Riner's campaign will fizzle out after a brief period of hype, and that the judoka will after all be a joker in the pack. But it is also possible that it won't, in which case the pre-election arithmetic will need a hasty readjustment: and it won't be the centrists who are smiling.

Thus far, Riner has shown himself a master of the codes required for this kind of out-of-nowhere candidacy, the first of which is to press home the message: "Don't Worry! I'm NOT a Politician!"

In this day and age in France, anyone who smacks of the "system" is automatically downgraded in voters' eyes, so it is important to emphasise that you are only running for office because, one, you have experienced real life (unlike those loafers in Paris); and two, you have discovered that there are solutions out there for the country's many problems. Solutions that are invisible to those same blinkered apparatchiks.

All this Riner was able to express in last Monday's social media broadcast by using sophisticated rhetorical devices.

"People say I am a fool for wanting to run for the presidency," he said.

"Am I a fool? Well, if refusing to see France sink under the weight of debt; refusing to see mothers and fathers grit their teeth every time they do their weekly shop, and tremble with fear when their kids go out on the street… if all that means being a fool, then yes call me a fool."

It was a promising oratorial start for the sportsman, and certainly attracted the viewers.

Are student protests being manipulated ahead of France's presidential election?

France's Marine Le Pen, fighting court conviction and running for presidency

But if he is serious – and Riner says he never does anything half-heartedly - that's not how he became an Olympic champion – then the hard work begins now.

What does Riner actually want to do? Who will be on his team? Where does he position himself on the all-consuming matters of the day: pension-reform, investment in education, the cost of living, public debt, the rise of populism or Russia's war in Ukraine?

In short, how does he intend to transform his undeniable popularity as a sporting figure into a political mandate?

Broadly, Riner appears to be on the right on economic matters and law and order, but being black and of Caribbean background he is also very strong on racism. When he says he is anti-extremism, he is referring mainly to Marine Le Pen.

In other words his pitch is somewhere in the centre, and against the extremes.

The trouble is, this is already an extremely crowded area, with important figures like ex-prime ministers Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal signally failing to take off.

Currently there are a dozen or so candidates in the area between centre right and centre left, stretching from the Socialist-backed Raphaël Glucksman to the Republicans' Bruno Retailleau on the right.

The latest possible addition is Christine Lagarde, who steps down as head of the European Central Bank next February.

The addition of yet another contender will dilute their polling numbers even further, making a second-round qualification for Mélenchon more likely.

So no wonder the leader of France Unbowed (LFI) seemed so happy about Riner's decision to run. "We know how it goes: neither right nor left means not left," Mélenchon told reporters on Friday.

The only other politician who seems genuinely pleased, rather than putting on a fixed smile, is President Emmanuel Macron, who said Riner was a "great champion" and that politics "did not belong to the professionals".

That could be explained by the president's cool relations with his former prime ministers, Philippe and Attal, both of whom are doing all they can to distance themselves from their unpopular one-time boss.

Riner said he viewed Macron's praise as a "poisoned chalice", telling reporters on Saturday that he was "not the president's envoy, I'm not a Macronist".

Politics and judo have very little in common, but of the two, as Riner will soon discover, the more vicious is not the one that is fought out hand-to-hand after mutual acknowledgement on the tatami mat.

If he starts looking like a serious candidate, Riner must know his life will be turned upside down, not just his physical form.

In politics you do not bow in respect to your opponent. You give him a metaphorical headbutt.

items.title: Tragedia al concerto di Elisa, una donna in prima fila si sente male e muore per arresto cardiaco
items.summary: È accaduto durante il raduno dei fan dell’artista all’Estragon Club a Bologna. La serata è stata annullata. L’organizzatore: “Momento terribile”
items.content:
Doveva essere una serata di festa e musica quella di sabato14 novembre. Ma si è trasformata in una tragedia. Una donna di 35 anni, nelle prime file del club Estragon di Bologna dove era in programma un concerto di Elisa , poco prima dell’inizio dello spettacolo, ha accusato un malore ed è stata immediatamente portata fuori dal locale in barella dai sanitari.

Stando al racconto di alcuni presenti, qualche minuto dopo Elisa è salita sul palco in lacrime e ha dato l’annuncio: “Purtroppo prima del concerto è successa una cosa gravissima, una fan ha avuto un arresto cardiaco e durante il trasporto in ospedale è morta. Eravamo qui per celebrare la vita, le connessioni, l'amicizia, tutte le cose belle, anche quelle brutte ma in maniera costruttiva, questo ci ricorda di quando tutto sia prezioso”.

L’appuntamento riservato al fan club dell’artista contava circa mille presenti ed è stato immediatamente sospeso.

Ci sono serate che vorresti non dover mai vivere – il post di Lele Roveri anima e organizzatore di ogni evento all’Estragon – sono quasi 35 anni che organizzo concerti. È il lavoro che ho scelto, la mia passione, una parte enorme della mia vita. In tutti questi anni ho visto passare davanti ai miei occhi centinaia di migliaia di persone. Persone che entrano in un locale o in un’arena con il sorriso, con l’entusiasmo di vedere il proprio artista preferito, con la voglia di cantare, ballare, incontrarsi, emozionarsi. E ogni volta, dietro alla gioia di vedere un locale pieno, dietro alla soddisfazione per un concerto riuscito, c’è sempre un grande senso di responsabilità. Una responsabilità che sento profondamente, oggi come il primo giorno». E continua:«Durante il raduno del fan club di Elisa all’Estragon, prima dell’inizio del concerto, una ragazza ha accusato un malore, un maledetto arresto cardiaco. È stata immediatamente assistita dal personale sanitario presente, portata in ospedale dove purtroppo è deceduta. Una ragazza che era venuta per condividere la passione per la sua artista preferita che non tornerà a casa. Non riesco a immaginare il dolore della sua famiglia, dei suoi amici, di chi la stava aspettando. E non ci sono parole che possano rendere meno terribile quello che è successo».

«Sono dovuto salire sul palco per dare la notizia – racconta Roveri – è stato un momento terribile. Insieme a Elisa abbiamo comunicato che la serata che non era ancora iniziata finiva lì, per tutti noi. In momenti come questo, tutto ciò che normalmente riempie le nostre giornate, i problemi, le preoccupazioni, le soddisfazioni, perde improvvisamente importanza. Rimane soltanto un dolore profondo e il pensiero di una vita spezzata troppo presto. A lei, alla sua famiglia e a tutte le persone che le volevano bene va il mio pensiero, il mio affetto e il mio abbraccio più sincero. Stasera la musica si è fermata. E il silenzio che rimane qui fuori all’Estragon, Parco Nord, è assordante».
